clue.text: Percussion made by water heater connected to taps?

parts.note: a kettle is the everyday appliance for heating water
to drum is to tap repeatedly with the fingers

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about some noise produced by a boiler hooked up to the plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taps' looks like plumbing beside the water heater, but it is a verb: drumming the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums are timpani, large tuned drums in the orchestra's percussion section.

clue.text: Calm down! You don't have to go topless!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom telling someone not to lose their temper

definitions.text: You don't have to go topless!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: taken literally, an instruction to stay clothed above the waist

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally the second time round.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal idiom urging someone to stay calm, and literally it means not removing one's top.

clue.text: Data set out includes note about lab explosion

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: Arranged data records a note on a laboratory blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is an arrangement of data in rows and columns, which is data laid out.

clue.text: Address temptation to keep jumble etc

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a lure is a temptation or enticement

indicators.note: a jumble is a muddle, so the letters next to it are mixed

parts.note: taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: A speech on temptation that keeps rambling on and so forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a place to send a letter, but it is a formal talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech to an audience, and a lecture is a talk of that kind.

clue.text: Put into confusion with grenade explosion

indicators.note: an explosion scatters its parts, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grenade going off throws everything into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or disturb the normal arrangement of something.

clue.text: They seize power from moneylenders supporting president

indicators.note: supporting means holding up, read here as holding the next letter within

parts.note: usurers lend money at extortionate interest
P is the abbreviation for president

explanation.surface: Coup leaders take control backed by moneylenders who stand behind the president.
explanation.walkthrough: The P sits inside the word for moneylenders, which is loosely signalled by 'supporting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurpers take a throne or authority illegally or by force, so they are people who grab power.

clue.text: Verbal blunder causing feelings to hot up

indicators.note: causing implies producing something new, so the letters after it are remade into another phrase

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless remark that makes tempers flare.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue is a minor error in speech, saying a wrong word by accident.

clue.text: Difficult about trial with being a bit deaf?

parts.note: hard means difficult
of can mean about, as in 'speak of'
a hearing is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A judge struggles during a trial because they can't quite hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard of hearing is the idiom for someone with partial loss of their hearing, i.e. somewhat deaf.

clue.text: Thoughtless in joining argument against team's right to tea break

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a con is a point against, as in pros and cons
a side is a sports team
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: A rude player complains that his team's tea interval was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea break' looks like a cricket interval; 'break' is the anagram signal on tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate means not thinking of others' feelings, a near synonym of thoughtless.

clue.text: Brie cooked in a small quantity is bitter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the mixed cheese sits inside the next part of the wordplay

parts.note: cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small measured quantity

indicators.note: cooking food transforms it, so the cheese's letters are mixed up

parts.note: the cheese, taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: A recipe note that a little cooked Brie tastes bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled cheese goes between the two Cs of cc, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic means sharp or sour in taste, and by extension cutting in manner, so it is a synonym of bitter.

clue.text: Right time to squeeze college for alumni get-together

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right

indicators.note: squeezing something means holding it tightly within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time
uni is short for university

explanation.surface: The right moment to cram a college in for a gathering of former students.
explanation.walkthrough: Uni is everyday British shorthand for university, and 'time' here means a long era.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion is a gathering of people, such as former classmates, meeting again after time apart.

clue.text: Go off ready to go on round-trip ticket

indicators.note: placed on means added after, so one piece follows the other
something that goes off has spoiled or exploded, so the following word's letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written before mixing
a go in a game is a turn

explanation.surface: An instruction to set out, ready for a trip there and back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off ready to go' reads like an instruction to leave; 'Go off' is the anagram signal and the second 'go' means a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A day return is a British railway ticket for travel out and back on the same day.

clue.text: Italian river is setting for sexy picture

indicators.note: a setting holds a gem, so the river surrounds the next word

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
hot is slang for sexy

explanation.surface: An Italian river makes the backdrop for a racy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Poultry's allegedly contaminated

indicators.note: allegedly means according to what people say, so we go by how a word is heard

parts.note: fowl are farmyard birds such as chickens

explanation.surface: A food scare: the chicken is said to be tainted.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul water or air is polluted or tainted, so the word is a synonym of contaminated.

clue.text: Honours special prices for famous people?

parts.note: a celeb is a celebrity; here it qualifies the prices, as in celeb rates
rates are set prices or charges

explanation.surface: A shop offering discounts to the famous, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, CELEB RATES: special prices for famous people. The definition is the verb at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To celebrate someone is to honour them publicly, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Strategy is to get guys hacked in to break local area network

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened word goes inside the next one

parts.note: a gap is a break or opening

indicators.note: hacked means chopped, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: guys are men
LAN is the standard abbreviation for local area network

explanation.surface: Cyber-criminals plot how to get into a computer network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacked' and 'network' suggest computers, but 'hacked' only means chopped short, and 'break' is a noun meaning an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is a carefully thought-out strategy for achieving an aim.

clue.text: Organise a giant sale of Fenland

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to arrange a huge sale in the Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying drained marshland in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: East Anglia is the region of eastern England containing most of the Fens, so it stands for Fenland here.

clue.text: Split the bill for travel from Holland

parts.note: to go is to travel
Dutch means coming from Holland

explanation.surface: A tourist wants to pay half the fare for a trip from the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each person paying their own share of a shared meal or outing.

clue.text: This month everything's put in place

parts.note: inst., instant, is the old business abbreviation for this month
all means everything

explanation.surface: This month everything has been set up.
explanation.walkthrough: In old business letters 'the 5th inst.' meant the fifth of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to fit or set it up in position, so it means put in place.

clue.text: Fine's overdue causing lengthy dispute

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
split as over due: the word due turned over, read backwards

explanation.surface: An unpaid library fine leading to a long-running quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overdue' must be split into two words, with 'over' telling you to turn the second one round.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a prolonged bitter quarrel, often between families, so it is a long-running dispute.

clue.text: Queen's greeting knight bearing flower

parts.note: R is short for regina, Latin for queen
hi is a casual greeting
N is the chess notation for knight
east is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: The Queen greets a knight who carries a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European river, and a river is a flower in the sense of a thing that flows.

clue.text: Having a low opinion of Princess's patronage

definitions.note: the answer is the noun, while the definition reads as an attitude; read as 'disapproval'

parts.note: Di, Princess Diana, plus the possessive S
favour is support or backing from a patron

explanation.surface: Someone disdains the support given by a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is Diana, Princess of Wales, a regular crossword princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Disfavour is disapproval or dislike, the state of thinking poorly of someone.

clue.text: Love short new dress

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to adore is to love
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone adores a short new frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a noun but is the verb, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn is to decorate or embellish, as one dresses a window or a tree.

clue.text: Short letter to public school about grant

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the school name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public (fee-paying) school
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: A brief letter sent to a school regarding funding.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is an elite private one; Eton is the classic example.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet for writing a brief message, so it carries a short letter.

clue.text: Between morning and last night song is composed

parts.note: a.m. denotes morning

indicators.note: composing means arranging afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written before mixing

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of night

explanation.surface: Between dawn and late evening a song gets written.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst is a variant of among, meaning in the midst of, which is close to between.

clue.text: Without a model Chanel cannot display calm

indicators.note: a display arranges things in a new way, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Without a model on the catwalk, Chanel can't show off composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests the catwalk beside Chanel, but here it is the Model T, giving one letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonchalance is casual unconcern, a relaxed composure, so it is a noun meaning calm.
